entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
bip-schnorr adopts an approach that always commits to the public key, ensuring signatures cannot be reused or manipulated in unintended ways. This design choice deliberately restricts flexibility, specifically disallowing certain use cases where not committing to the public key might be desirable. The motivation for this restriction has grown stronger following recent incidents of signature misuse, such as the fake Satoshi signature controversy, highlighting the importance of robust cryptographic practices to prevent abuse.
While these constraints may limit some legitimate applications, alternative mechanisms remain available for advanced scripting and functionality within Bitcoin. Solutions like covenants can be implemented through OP_CHECKSIGFROMSTACK, as detailed in [this research paper](https://fc17.ifca.ai/bitcoin/papers/bitcoin17-final28.pdf). Another proposal, OP_PUSHTXDATA, is discussed in [this BIP draft](https://github.com/jl2012/bips/blob/vault/bip-0ZZZ.mediawiki), offering further possibilities for enhancing transaction logic.
These developments are positioned as logical progressions after the Taproot soft fork, suggesting a path forward for expanding Bitcoin’s capabilities while maintaining security and integrity in signature schemes.
